followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified math problem with a clear, single correct answer — the kind of task either model can handle. I routed it based on capability rather than task preference, since there's nothing distasteful or open-ended here to engage the models' differing preference profiles.

On the numbers: Willet-235B scores higher on the general reasoning and knowledge benchmarks most relevant to a number theory problem (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA Diamond 64.1 vs 56.2, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 83.2). Those gaps are well outside run-to-run variance and point to stronger quantitative reasoning, which is exactly what this units-digit problem rewards.

Lapwing actually *prefers* well-specified tasks like this one, but its documentation explicitly notes that preference is dissociated from capability — preferring a task doesn't make it answer better. So the preference signal isn't a reason to override the capability advantage.

Willet was the straightforward pick.
